senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; נָפַח or פּוּחַ)that which is used for kindling, charcoal.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 2:5">Sabb. II, 5</cite> <he>מפני שהוא עושה פ׳</he> because (by extinguishing the light) he makes kindling material, i.e. prepares the wick for easier lighting (v. <cite ref="E00029"><he>הִבְהֵב</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 9:8:1">Koh. R. to IX, 8</cite> <he>נפח לפֶחָמוֹ</he> the smith (the charcoal-burner) turns to his coal.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:1">Ib. to VII, 1</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 35">Yalk. Josh. 35</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q00313"><he>פּוּצָם</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="Q00477"><he>פֶּחָמִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00451"><he>פֶּי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 5:13">Tosef. Maas. Sh. V, 13</cite>; Y. ib. V, beg. 55ᵈ, v. <cite ref="Q00478"><he>פָּחַם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Beitsah 3:14">Tosef. Bets. III, 14</cite> <he>אין עושין פ׳ וכ׳</he> you must not make charcoal (prepare kindling material) even for immediate use (on the Holy Day).

<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 9:2">Mikv. IX, 2</cite> <he>לא יטבול … בפ׳ וכ׳</he> one must not immerse a kettle with remnants of coal in it (which had been put there to be extinguished in water), unless one washes it again, Maim.; [oth. opin.: with the soot on it, but he must scrape it off].

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:8:4">Koh. R. to I, 8</cite> <he>לכו … האיש ועל אותה החמת … מלאה פ׳</he> go ye and pray for this man (me), and for this bag formerly filled with precious stones and pearls, and now with pieces of coal; a. e.
